title: Wesley Gilbert
description: Biophysicist and engineer working at the intersection of synthetic biology, computational biophysics, and semiconductor infrastructure.

about.short: I'm a biophysicist and engineer chasing problems at the edge of what's possible — from the mechanics of living cells to the manufacturing of next-generation chips.
about.extended: My work spans synthetic biology, computational biophysics, and semiconductor packaging. I build open-source tools, write about the science, and try to leave every system I touch more understandable than I found it.

focus_areas.title: Synthetic Biology
focus_areas.description: Genetic engineering, lipid nanoparticle delivery systems, and the molecular machinery of living cells. Currently developing open-source tools for LNP formulation prediction.

focus_areas.title: Computational Biophysics
focus_areas.description: Finite element analysis of bone remodeling, cellular mechanobiology, and the numerical methods that turn biology into tractable equations.

focus_areas.title: Systems & Infrastructure
focus_areas.description: Disaggregated semiconductor packaging at Intel, containerized APIs, cloud deployment, and the engineering discipline of making complex systems reliable at scale.
